name: Raga
description: District headquarters and main town of Kamle district, serving as the primary gateway and administrative hub for exploring the surrounding hills, forests, and river valleys of central Arunachal Pradesh.
facts: Headquarters of Kamle district, created in 2017 from parts of Lower and Upper Subansiri
Located approximately 44 km north of Ziro and about 100 km from Itanagar
Main population center and starting point for local tourism and cultural experiences among Nyishi communities
Coordinates from Wikipedia and geographic records

name: Daporijo
description: Headquarters of Upper Subansiri district, a remote riverside town on the Subansiri River known for its hanging bridges, tribal markets, and as the gateway to unexplored northern valleys and border areas.
facts: District headquarters of Upper Subansiri, elevation about 600 m on the banks of Subansiri River
Famous for the strategic Daporijo Bridge and traditional bamboo hanging bridges
Gateway to Taksing, Limeking, Nacho and remote Tagin tribal areas near the India-China border
Coordinates from Wikipedia; limited tourist infrastructure makes it an authentic offbeat experience

name: Menga Mandir (Meghna Cave Temple)
description: Ancient rock cave temple dedicated to Lord Shiva (Lakulisha) with natural tunnels and a Shiva Linga, located near the confluence of Subansiri and Mengha rivers about 22 km north of Daporijo.
facts: Rock cave temple with two tunnels requiring crawling in places; natural Shiva Linga inside
Officially listed as a place of interest by Upper Subansiri district administration; best time Oct-Feb
Located 22 km north of Daporijo towards Taliha near river confluence
Approximate coordinates from cave databases and local mapping; sacred site visited especially during Shivratri

name: Taksing
description: Remote border village and circle headquarters near the India-China Line of Actual Control on the Subansiri River, offering snow-clad mountain views, Tagin tribal culture, and access to sacred Takpa Siri pilgrimage trails.
facts: Circle headquarters near McMahon Line; road connectivity improved by BRO in 2018
Inhabited by Tagin people; traditional trade and pilgrimage routes including to Takpa Siri (Dakpa Sheri) sacred mountain
Coordinates from Wikipedia; high-altitude remote area ideal for adventure trekking in winter
Best visited in winter for snow views; requires special permits due to border proximity

name: Limeking
description: Remote high-altitude village and circle headquarters known for organic apple and kiwi orchards, orchid-rich forests, and as the starting point for multi-day treks to Gegu Seria Lake.
facts: About 143 km from Daporijo; one of the most remote villages with limited connectivity
Home to organic fruit orchards and rich biodiversity including orchids
Starting point for 4-day trek to Gegu Seria Lake on mountain top
Coordinates from Wikipedia; elevation around 2000 m

name: Nacho
description: Peaceful hill village about 65 km north of Daporijo, surrounded by terraced fields and forests, serving as a base for local treks including to Mengva Cave Temple and nearby viewpoints like Charu.
facts: Located 65 km north of Daporijo; Tagin tribal village with terraced agriculture
Base for adventure activities including trekking and rafting on Subansiri
Nearby attractions include Charu Village viewpoint and Mengva Cave Temple
Coordinates from Wikipedia; emerging destination management focus by district administration

name: Ligu Village
description: Rural tourism hub just 3-4 km from Daporijo offering authentic Tagin tribal homestays, cultural performances, and traditional lifestyle experiences in a village-operated setting.
facts: Official rural tourism site with community-run homestays showcasing Tagin heritage
Located only 3-4 km from Daporijo headquarters
Best time November to February; ideal for cultural immersion without long travel
Source: District Upper Subansiri official places of interest

name: Gegu Seria Lake
description: Beautiful natural high-altitude lake on a mountain top, reachable only by a challenging four-day trek from Limeking through remote forests and ridges.
facts: Requires four days of trekking from Limeking; located on mountain top
Officially listed as a place of interest by the district administration
Pristine and rarely visited; best time November to February
Source: uppersubansiri.nic.in places of interest

name: Subansiri River
description: Major trans-Himalayan tributary of the Brahmaputra flowing through Upper Subansiri, offering angling, white-water rafting (especially from Nacho), and scenic riverside landscapes amid dense forests.
facts: Largest tributary of the Brahmaputra; enters India near Taksing
Official adventure tourism: angling throughout, rafting from Nacho downstream
Lifeline of the district supporting tribal communities and scenic views
Best for water sports in winter (Nov-Feb)

name: Dumporijo
description: Village east of Daporijo home to the Aato Topo statue commemorating the forefather of the Topo clan, along with traditional Tagin settlements and cultural significance.
facts: About 15 km east of Daporijo; site of Aato Topo statue built in 2004
Aato Topo is regarded as the forefather of the Topo clan among Tagin people
Coordinates approximate from GeoNames and mapping sources
Listed in Wikipedia tourism notes for Upper Subansiri

name: Charu Village
description: Small mountain-top village about 7 km from Nacho offering panoramic views of Nacho town, floating clouds below, and distant snow-capped peaks; ideal for quiet rural tourism.
facts: Located on a mountain top approximately 7 km from Nacho
Sparse population with stunning vistas of surrounding valleys and peaks
Featured in district destination spotlight for emerging tourism
Source: Upper Subansiri Destination Management Committee newsletter

name: Nogotum Waterfall
description: Scenic waterfall located just before Nacho near Garam Village under Siyum Circle, approximately 1 km from the main highway, offering a peaceful natural spot for visitors.
facts: Located in Garam Village, about 1 km off the highway before Nacho
Under Siyum Circle; relatively unexplored by mainstream tourists
Highlighted in official destination management materials for Upper Subansiri
Best visited during post-monsoon for full flow

name: Sippi Valley
description: Fertile green valley near Daporijo dotted with rice fields, waterfalls, traditional bamboo huts, and lush forests, popular for nature walks, photography, and camping.
facts: Known for fertile lands, rice fields, and traditional bamboo architecture
Mentioned among top attractions around Daporijo for greenery and waterfalls
Suitable for riverside and hillside camping
Source: travel accounts and district tourism notes

name: Taliha
description: Circle headquarters village north of Daporijo serving as a base for trekking, hiking, and rock-climbing in the surrounding rugged terrain and nearby villages.
facts: Officially recommended for trekking, hiking and rock-climbing activities
Located on the route towards northern valleys and Nacho
Part of the adventure tourism circuit in Upper Subansiri
Source: District administration places of interest
